sexual minority women's interactions with their breast cancer physicians can be positive or negative depending on the physician's attitudes and behaviors, and that these attitudes and behaviors can be learned and improved.

the quality of patient-physicians' interactions and the factors that contribute to patient satisfaction with their care.
the quality of care sexual minority women receive from their treating physicians.

satisfaction of sexual minority breast cancer patients with their physicians is connected with a particular style of interactions rather than physician's gender.
sexual minority women are satisfied with their breast cancer treatment if they perceive their treating physicians as being caring, supportive, and respectful.
sexual minority women's satisfaction with breast cancer care depends on the physician's ability to create an environment that is conducive to patient-centered care.
